question: In which language was 'Mudraraksha' play written by Vishakhadatta?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanskrit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Mudraraksha'** is a historical Sanskrit play written by **Vishakhadatta**.
 
• The play is believed to have been written between the **4th and 8th centuries CE**.
 
• It depicts the political and administrative strategies employed during the reign of the **Mauryan Empire**, particularly around the time of **Chandragupta Maurya**.
 
• The narrative revolves around the clever diplomacy of **Chanakya (Kautilya)** to dethrone the Nanda dynasty and establish Chandragupta Maurya as the ruler.
 
• 'Mudraraksha' translates to "The Signet Ring of Rakshasa," referring to the role of Rakshasa, the loyal minister of the Nanda dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sanskrit Literature:**

 
 
• Sanskrit is one of the oldest languages in the world and forms the basis of classical Indian literature.
 
• It has a rich tradition of plays, poetry, epics, and philosophical texts like the Vedas, Upanishads, and epics like Mahabharata and Ramayana.
 
 
 
• **Chanakya:**
 
 
• Also known as Kautilya or Vishnugupta, he was a celebrated strategist and the author of the treatise **Arthashastra**.
 
• He played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Mauryan Empire.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context of 'Mudraraksha':**
 
 
• The play provides insight into the political dynamics and strategies used during ancient Indian history.
 
• It highlights themes of loyalty, power, and statecraft.
 
 
 
• **Mauryan Empire:**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire (322–185 BCE) was one of the largest empires in ancient India, founded by Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• It reached its peak under Emperor Ashoka, known for his propagation of Buddhism and the Edicts of Ashoka.
